title: Concentric Circle Stitch: isosceles Triangle, round 6
description: PE-DESIGN 11.50's Concentric Circle Stitch, round 6: circles about the centre one row apart. With the start point on a whole circle the whole circles go first, outside in, then the cut ones after a trim; with the start point beyond the whole circles (portrait shapes, a triangle's corner) PE starts there on the cut circles and works inwards to the middle. PE: starts at the bottom-left corner (-19.9,+19.4) and ends at the centre: the cut circles first, outside in. The seam is not compared. Open, pinned at the internal tier: stitches (PE 1283, OpenStitch 1383).

references.make: Shapes > isosceles Triangle dragged (30,30)-(70,70) mm; region Concentric Circle Stitch. Hoop 100 x 100 mm page; line Not Sewn (Line); colour 800 EMBROIDERY RED; region attributes at their defaults (Density 2,0 line/mm, Run pitch 2,0 mm, Start Point first button) unless stated; nothing else in the design. Save As PES (default type, #PES0110). Status bar 40,00 x 39,50 mm, 1283 st.

measurements.evidence: KNOWN DIFFERENCE (open): PE-DESIGN 11.50's file measures 1283, OpenStitch 1383; this check pins OpenStitch's value until the rule is found: PE-DESIGN's per-circle needle counts grow about linearly with the radius (2·π·r / pitch plus about 20 extra split stitches) where OpenStitch uses 4·2^n points; the gap shows most on small circles and on squares (COMPATIBILITY_AUDIT, Concentric Circle and Spiral).
